summary: All five supplied occurrences checked. 30/83, 49/6 and both Talay 1/97 forms are already represented in the entry; their thin-cell proposals do not warrant duplicates.

Praise can have a b-marked praised person, while esteem has zero-marked Gospel, Christ and Mary. Neutral description at 74/26 has content plus recipient -le and then an ayko indirect question; this is a meaning distinction, not merely a different object type.
The new description sense rests on one source verse with a repeated predicate. No dialectal or contact-development history beyond the inherited Arabic etymology is inferred.

Round 2 only. Jan English is a project machine translation, not an edition translation; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are inherited in the reading layout and are not repeated in this JSON.
Direct ruḥe and b ruḥi mark self-praise without creating a separate lexical sense. The modesty/disclaimer context supports praise despite the machine translation describing.
Mwaṣafnolox has a recipient -lox in a praise context; l-recipient alone therefore does not distinguish round-1 neutral description from praise.
Three new contexts fill II Infectum sense 1 from two inherited examples to five; the paired craft predicates are quoted together once.

Does neutral description also accept the b-marked content found with praise, or is it restricted to a direct content object/indirect question plus l-recipient? Further speaker evidence would clarify the valency boundary.
Confirm whether mawṣəf ruḥe (Jan 2.4/581) is specifically self-praise or neutral self-description, and whether maw-/mw- is orthographic variation in II.
Positive family recommendation and praise of one’s own craft retain laudatory sense 1. Jan does not securely add neutral-description evidence to round-1 sense 2.
